newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's power consumption rises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's power consumption rises in 1996.

text.p: Bulgaria's electricity consumption rose by 1.3 percent to some 42.4 billion kilowatt hours in 1996 despite drastic price hikes, energy officials said on Saturday.
The National Elecetricity Company said it had not yet evaluated last year's industrial and domestic consumption but a rise in domestic consumption was expected.
The Energy Ministry announced power price increases of 43.8 percent for January. The rising cost of electricity and coal is stretching budgets economy during the cold winter.
Energy officials said international lending institutions had recommended a target electricity rate of 3.5 cents per kilowatt hour, while it was currently less than three cents.
Since July, energy prices have been revised each month, mainly according to the inflation rate and the lev/dollar exchange rate.

The lev fell from 70 to the dollar at the beginning of 1996 to some 650 on Saturday. Bulgaria imports more than 80 percent of raw materials for its energy sector and pays for the supplies after it exchanges levs for dollars.
Bulgarian electricity output last year rose to 42.9 billion kilowatt hours from 42 billion kilowatt hours following a constant tendency in recent years.
Electricity production was 30.9 billion kilowatt hours in 1992, 33.1 billion kilowatt hours in 1993, 33.6 billion kilowatt hours in 1994 and 37.4 billion kilowatt hours in 1995.

The ministry said output structure improved in 1996 with a big increase in the share of the production of the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, whose annual output reached 18.8 billion kilowatt hours against 17.3 billion kilowatt hours in 1995.
